title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The document titled “Decision of the AI Office” records a formal ruling issued by the AI Office. It outlines the decision’s purpose, the key points considered, and the expected effects on stakeholders and policy implementation.

summary: This policy outlines the availability of AI office positions for technology specialists. It explains the qualifications, roles, and application process for those interested in pursuing these AI-related opportunities.

summary: The document announces a vacancy for a Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office. It outlines the main responsibilities of the role and the qualifications and experience needed for candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy outlines the responsibilities and qualifications for a vacant AI Office position within the Legal Officers department. It details the hiring process, expectations for managing AI-related legal compliance, and how the role supports organizational governance.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The document announces a vacancy for AI policy officers, outlining the duties and qualifications required for individuals to oversee AI governance within the organization. It stresses that these roles are crucial for developing ethical AI policies and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts that advises lawmakers on how scientific and technical evidence should shape the EU’s AI regulation. It reviews the risks and benefits of AI systems, recommends safeguards, and helps ensure the Act’s rules are grounded in current research and best practices.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This document proposes a framework for standardising AI development and deployment practices. It outlines the key areas where uniform standards are needed, such as safety, transparency, and data governance.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This document announces a consultation concerning a Community of Practice (CoP) initiative. It invites stakeholders to share their views and provide input to help shape the CoP’s development and implementation.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The policy document announces a call for individuals or organizations to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI policy and related issues. It outlines the purpose of the CoP, the benefits of participation, and provides details on how to submit an expression of interest and contact information.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document explains how a Community of Practice (CoP) uses an iterative drafting process to create and refine AI policy documents. It outlines the steps for gathering stakeholder input, reviewing drafts, making revisions, and finalizing the policy to ensure clarity, compliance, and inclusivity.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The graphic outlines the step‑by‑step timeline of drafting the Community of Practice policy, showing each phase from initial proposal to final approval. It highlights key milestones, dates, and the parties responsible at each stage of the drafting process.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 1st Draft outlines guidelines for developing and deploying AI responsibly, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and ethical considerations. It provides best practices for stakeholders to ensure AI systems are safe, fair, and aligned with societal values.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft outlines guidelines and best practices for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence. It emphasizes ethical principles, transparency, accountability, and risk management to promote responsible and trustworthy AI systems.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document presents the third version of a set of guidelines designed to help organizations use AI responsibly. It outlines key principles, standards, and procedures that should be followed to ensure ethical, safe, and compliant AI deployment.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework for ensuring responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies. It outlines commitments to transparency, safety, fairness, and international cooperation among governments, industry, and civil society to mitigate risks and promote benefits.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a finalised agreement that outlines how organizations should responsibly develop, use, and govern AI systems. It sets out key principles such as transparency, fairness, safety, and accountability, and establishes shared responsibilities, monitoring mechanisms, and enforcement measures to ensure AI technologies are used ethically and responsibly.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This document lists the types of AI actions, techniques, and uses that are explicitly forbidden, offering clear examples and explanations of each prohibited practice. It serves as a guide for developers and users to avoid activities that violate ethical guidelines and regulatory requirements.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: The Guidelines on AI System Definition offer a clear framework for identifying and categorizing artificial intelligence systems. They outline criteria such as functionality, scope, and potential impact to help organizations classify AI products and ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines how the organization will communicate initiatives designed to support the growth of start‑ups and spur innovation. It covers strategies for engaging stakeholders, sharing best practices, and building a collaborative ecosystem to accelerate new business development.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is designed to help early‑stage companies in the high‑performance computing industry across Europe. It offers resources, mentorship and funding to accelerate the development and commercialization of HPC technologies.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar will cover risk management strategies for AI, focusing on identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential hazards. Attendees will learn best practices for governance, compliance, and continuous monitoring to ensure safe AI deployment.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar explores risk management strategies for AI, outlining how to identify, assess, and mitigate potential threats. It stresses the need for ongoing oversight, transparent processes, and adaptive policies to safeguard users and maintain system integrity.
